## What's in it
- Everything in both spec documents is implemented: movement, all space types, events, shops, items and spellbooks, equipment, skills, 9 classes, battles, co-op Demon Lord Army fights, hero duels, the roaming minion, bots, 4 save slots, and all 3 endings with the dialogue from game_dialogue.md.
- All pictures and models are drawn in code: 9 classes × 2 genders, 13 monsters and bosses with Thai flavour (the Kong Koi Ghost hops on one leg, the mummy wears headphones), buildings including a Thai-style temple, and scenery for each zone. Music and sound effects are synthesised with the Web Audio API.
- The LocalStorage schema is in docs/localstorage_schema.md: 4 slots, an autosave, settings and lifetime records, all under the soleblessed:v1: key prefix, with versioning.
- CLAUDE.md covers the architecture, conventions, and every place where I had to interpret the spec.

## Testing
- node tools/test-rules.js: 31 checks of the spec's rules (damage table, cooldowns, EXP, level-ups). All pass.
- node tools/simulate.js: plays full games with 4 bots and checks the game state after every turn. No errors across hundreds of games.
- I drove the real page in headless Chrome, both desktop and phone size. That covered a complete game from start to ending, 18 days of keyboard play as a human, and save → exit → load. It caught three bugs, which are fixed.
- Not verified: how the audio actually sounds, real touch devices, and Safari/iOS.

## Decision for you: the spec's balance can't reach the Demon Lord
In simulation, the Demon Lord is almost never defeated in 35 days with the spec's EXP numbers. Heroes are around level 17 on day 30, while he is level 28 behind three Generals, so games nearly always end Bad.

I didn't change the spec's numbers. Instead, the character creation screen has a Rules option:

| Setting | Demon Lord defeated | Endings |
|---|---|---|
| 35 days · Classic (default, exact spec) | ~0–3% of games | almost always Bad |
| 45 days · Brisk (EXP ×1.5, heroes heal 10% HP each morning), the "★ Recommended" button | ~50–70% of games | good mix of Good / Secret / Bad |

These results are with 4 bots; a human player should do somewhat better. Tell me which one should be the default.

## Spec fixes and interpretations
- Zone 2's t01 has no connecting line in the layout, so nobody could ever reach it. I connected it to e14 directly below it.
- The spec's bot rules made bots stall, so I added small, documented fixes. For example, low-HP bots only retreat if they can afford healing, because temples don't heal and broke bots looped forever.

The rest are listed in CLAUDE.md.

Rebalance:
- Monsters: each zone has 3 monster types, weaker near the zone entrance and stronger near the General. That adds 4 new monsters: Mischievous Monkey, Striped Tiger, Sand Wyrm and Lava Golem.
- Enemy levels follow your zone bands (1–12, 13–24, 24–36, 37–50). Generals are Lv 12, 24 and 36, and the Demon Lord is Lv 50.
- Gear: there are now 8 equipment tiers, 2 per zone. Charms give percentage bonuses so they stay useful late, and there's a new Jade Amulet charm (Max HP +10%).
- Items and money: there's a new Royal Elixir (full heal), and treasure and event money grow with the zone.
- How I tuned it: I added tools/balance.js, which simulates fights to set enemy HP and attack. At the level you first meet them, monsters take about one day to beat and cost about 30% of your HP.

Decisions to check. These are my readings of the parts of your list that were ambiguous:
1. "The fight still goes on": if you team up against a monster, the heroes still standing must duel each other once it dies. If you attack the hero instead, the duel winner takes over the monster fight. Fights against the Generals, Demon Lord and minion stay co-op, with no forced duel afterwards.
2. "2 days" to resurrect or stand up means skipping your next 2 turns.
3. Forced battle screen: since the inventory is no longer reachable before an unfinished fight, you use your once-per-turn item from an O Item button inside the battle (healing items and Energy Drink only).
4. Exact steps: stepping onto a General or the Demon Lord's Castle still ends your move there, even with steps left. Otherwise bosses could only be reached with a perfect roll.
5. Log button during bot turns: it stays usable, like Pause, because it only shows information.
6. Challenge Letter: using it moves you to the target's space, the duel starts immediately, and it uses up your turn.

Old saves: saves from the first version can't be loaded because the map changed. They show as "older version" and can only be deleted.

King's Requests, victory poses and the results sharing (image card plus copyable text) are in, as are all the screen and UI changes you listed. The updated spec is docs/project_spec.md; it opens with a changelog, and its tables are checked against the game data. docs/localstorage_schema.md and CLAUDE.md are updated too.

- Git attribution rule: commit messages end with Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
- Script and state architecture
- Pure HTML/CSS/JS with classic <script> tags that share a global lexical scope. No ES modules, so file:// works.
- Load order: util, data, save, audio, sprites, map, game, battle, bot, ui, main.
- Async/await turn loop. Game.wait(ms) handles speed, pause, skip, and ABORT via runId.
- Decision parity: Game.who(p) returns Bot or UI, which share method names.
- Single JSON Game.state, persisted to localStorage (prefix soleblessed:v1:, SAVE_SCHEMA 2).
- Headless simulation: Game.sim = true, SimView, UI stubbed as global.UI = {}. Node loads the files with vm.runInThisContext.
- Rendering and audio
- Canvas 2.5D projection with TILT = 0.6.
- The land layer is cached in an offscreen canvas; roads, tiles and objects are drawn live and depth-sorted.
- Procedural sprites; Web Audio synth for music and SFX.
- Map parsing and movement
- ASCII map parsing: codes every 5 characters; │ accepted when i % 5 <= 2; duplicate codes renamed.
- Exact-step move search: MapSys.exactMoves(prefix, steps, isBlocking) is a DFS with a budget that returns {ends: Map, next: Set}.
- Space depth (0 at entrance, 1 at General) drives monster tiers.
- Persistent battles
- Battle kinds: monster, army and duel.
- reserve and resume implement brawls; the post-monster duel happens after a monster falls.
- Down-state: p.down = 2 turns after a KO or giving up.
- Game systems

- exactMoves(prefix, steps, isBlocking, cap):
       function exactMoves(prefix, steps, isBlocking, cap) {
         const ends = new Map(), next = new Set();
         const path = prefix.slice(), onPath = new Set(path), base = path.length;
         let budget = cap || 300000;
         const last = path[path.length - 1];
         if (path.length > 1 && isBlocking(last)) { ends.set(last, path.slice()); return { ends, next }; }
         if (steps <= 0) { if (path.length > 1) ends.set(last, path.slice()); return { ends, next }; }
         const found = () => { if (!ends.has(path[path.length - 1])) ends.set(path[path.length - 1], path.slice()); next.add(path[base]); };
         (function dfs(cur, left) {
           for (const n of spaces[cur].links) {
             if (onPath.has(n) || --budget < 0) continue;
             path.push(n); onPath.add(n);
             if (isBlocking(n) || left === 1) found();
             else dfs(n, left - 1);
             path.pop(); onPath.delete(n);
           }
         })(last, steps);
         return { ends, next };
       }

1. Standing up after giving up (or resurrecting). Two things could pull a hero into a fight before they got to move:
- If a Demon Lord Army fight was still going on their space, pressing roll opened a "Join the battle / Roll" prompt instead of rolling. Bots in that spot joined automatically.
- The minion could ambush them at the end of the day, before their turn came round.

Now the first turn after resting always goes straight to rolling. Until that turn ends, nobody can challenge that hero and the minion won't ambush them, even if a fight, another hero or the minion is on the same space.

3. Shop details covering the arrows. The details box now sits on the left, just above the destination box, and no longer touches the arrows.

I've made a fix for the phone sound, but I couldn't test it on a real iPhone, so please check it after you push. It's committed locally as 48a5548.

Most likely cause: silent mode. When an iPhone's ring/silent switch is on silent, iOS mutes the kind of audio the game uses (every sound is generated live in code). Videos and music still play in silent mode, which makes it look like only the game is broken. The game now tells iOS to treat it like a video or music app, so sound plays even in silent mode. On older iPhones it does this by quietly looping a silent clip in the background.

Two smaller problems, also fixed:
- Tapping the map didn't start the sound. iOS only allows a page to start sound from a completed tap, and the map was trying to start it on the first finger-down. Now any tap, click or key press anywhere turns the sound on.
- Sound could stay off after a call or switching apps. iOS leaves the sound in a paused state the game didn't recognise. The game now restarts it on your next tap.

What I tested: in Chrome, both as desktop and pretending to be an iPhone, a single tap starts the sound, the music plays, and the silent clip loads and loops. It pauses when you leave the page and restarts on your next tap. The rule tests and simulator still pass.

Please check after pushing:
1. Open the game on your iPhone with silent mode on and tap once on the title screen. The title music should start.
2. Try the Instagram in-app browser too, since you played there before. It sometimes has stricter audio rules than Safari.
3. If there's still no sound, tell me your iOS version and whether it's Safari or Instagram.

Since sound now plays in silent mode, you'd use the music and sound-effect sliders in Settings to mute it.
